items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: I'm not a real good friend of Raymond Burke at all. I just know him.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I got to know, well, there were so many good clients in New Orleans during the time I was down there digging. I once marched in a parade. The only parade I ever marched was in the evening, during the Marley Grove, in New Orleans. The same Johnny Brent got me the job, and they had, in this band, they had Azola, they had Nina Pekona, they had Myer Weinberg, who was Gene Meyer, I think he calls himself now. They just had all of the jazz…
I want to ask you some technical things, since you sold instruments. Oh, yeah. And reeds and all that. How hard a reed would people use in those days?
